The National Regulatory Authorities of Greece and Cyprus approved the submitted Investment Request for the Project and agreed on the CBCA between them. The decision "Cross-Border Cost Allocation Between the Hellenic Regulatory Authority for Energy (RAE) and the Cyprus Energy Regulatory Authority (CERA)" provided on 10th of October 2017 concerned the implementation of PCIs 3.10.2 & 3.10.3. With the corresponding decision for PCI 3.10.1 not yet received, and to avoid delays in the implementation of the Project and to be in line with the obligations and commitments arising from the CBCA approval, the Project Promoter decided to amend the order of implementation of the three PCIs consisting PCI 3.10 as follows, with PCIs 3.10.2 & 3.10.3 implemented concurrently: PCI 3.10.3 Interconnection between Korakia, Crete and Attica region(EL) PCI 3.10.2 Interconnection between Kofinou (CY) and Korakia, Crete (EL) PCI 3.10.1 Interconnection between Hadera (IL) and Kofinou (CY)

The project programme was delayed comparing to the initial application for TYNDP 2016 due to two main factors. Firstly, the studies performed in conjunction with National Grid in order to determine a connection location in the UK, which commenced at the time of the application for TYNDP 2016, took longer time than expected. The studies were successfully completed in the late 2015. Secondly, two connection points were initially suggested in France - Le Havre and Barnabos. Further studies were required to determine the point of connection with the least impact on the national transmission system and greater feasibility of implementation. As an outcome, AQUIND accepted the PTF from RTE in respect of Barnabos substation. The project promoter commenced the studies with National Grid and RTE approximately at the same time as applying for TYNDP 2016 and at that stage such circumstances were not foreseeable.

LEG1 has been rescheduled to allow for 150 MW solar power plant (comprising energy storage) to be developped. GreenPower2020 feel this is necessary for 2 reasons: 1. to test and to qualify technologies in a given environment (hence not duplicating previous errors from others) and to identify the appropriate combination (PV + battery, CSP + steam, ...) before the utility-scale deployment of 2 x 1 GW. 2. To include energy generation as part of the project to enable LEG1's bi-lateral power exchange capability immediately.

The PCI was delayed due to regulatory processes in the Republic of Ireland which have now been remedied. The Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU), on 21 October 2017, directed EirGrid to progress grid applications from interconnectors with PCI status, including Greenlink; also the CRU issued an information paper on 21 March 2018 acknowledging Greenlink’s application and setting out the timeframe to develop, consult, and make an initial decision on, Greenlink’s application by 30 September 2018.

Maali was listed and recommend for inclusion in the PCI list at the TEN-E regional groups meeting in Brussels 27th June 2017, however it was not supported by all member states in a closed meeting on 13th July due to a proposal to connect Shetland to Scotland with a 60MW distribution cable which would not have supported Maali. The 60MW connection was subsequently rejected by the GB Regulator Ofgem on 30th November 2018 opening the way for the planned >=600MW connection to Scotland and facilitating the connection of Maali.
